title: Polar alignment reports error in raw arcseconds ("1800.0 arcseconds", "Up 2287.9\""), which no one adjusting a wedge can read
summary: Added one shared formatter, formatPolarError, that follows the magnitude the way NINA/SharpCap do: arcseconds with a decimal under 1', arcmin+arcsec under 1 degree, degrees+arcmin+arcsec above that, sign preserved, non-finite rendered as '--'. Wired into every readout that previously printed a raw arcsecond count: the Adjust Mount az/alt/total tiles and its threshold caption, the right-rail Azimuth/Altitude/Total tiles, the completion headline (both the 'Final error' and 'Still N off' branches), the Before/After summary boxes, the history rows, and the All-Sky reticle caption. The fixed 30"/60"/120" ring labels on the bullseye were deliberately left in arcseconds — that is the regime where the arcsecond IS the unit.
test: polar_alignment_error_format_test.dart (6 unit cases incl. the 2287.9" -> 38' 08" and 40104" -> 11 deg 08' 24" the audit saw, plus the 3599.7" carry and sign/NaN handling) and polar_alignment_wizard_ux_test.dart 'a run that reached its target reads in arcminutes' / 'a run that missed its target reads in arcminutes too'.
revert_check: Reverted _completion_panel.dart:57 to `'Final error: ${state.currentError!.totalError.toStringAsFixed(1)} arcseconds'` — polar_alignment_wizard_ux_test fails; restored — passes.

The button also carries a tooltip saying where the panel appears. The panel stays where it is structurally — the defect was that the toggle's only effect was below the fold, not where the panel lives.

title: Polar alignment config controls stay visually enabled during a run but silently ignore clicks
summary: The controls were already genuinely disabled (every callback is `isRunning ? null : ...`), so the defect was purely that nothing said so: SegmentedButton.styleFrom used the same surfaceAlt for enabled and disabled, so the column kept full contrast. The column now shows a 'Settings are locked while aligning — press Stop to change them.' note above the groups while a run is in flight, and the three settings groups dim to the muted opacity token. Kept above the disabled threshold so the operator can still READ the hemisphere/binning the run is using.

title: Re-opening Polar Alignment shows the previous run's "Alignment Complete" screen instead of a fresh start
summary: polarAlignmentStateProvider is app-scoped, so Done (which pops to Imaging) left the terminal state standing and re-entry landed on the old completion summary with Restart as the only way back to the instructions. The screen now releases a FINISHED run on dispose: only phase complete/error, via a post-frame callback (mutating a provider inside dispose lands mid-teardown), and a PolarAlignmentBusyException is swallowed so an in-flight history save is never forced. A run still in flight is untouched — coming back to a live measurement must show it. The controller and phase are snapshotted each build because `ref` is invalid inside a ConsumerState dispose.
test: 'leaving a finished run reopens the wizard on idle' — pops the wizard and asserts the provider phase is idle and that re-entry shows neither 'Alignment Stopped' nor 'Alignment Complete'.
revert_check: Removed the `_releaseFinishedRun();` call from dispose() — test fails (phase stays complete); restored — passes.

title: All-Sky alignment shows a drift-derived error with no indication of how long the drift baseline is
summary: Split the finding. The measurable half is fixed: the All-Sky readout now carries 'Drift baseline: 4m 12s' under the az/alt/total tiles, computed from the exact interval the misalignment was derived over — state.initialError is the FIRST drift solve of the adjustment phase and state.currentError the latest, so their timestamp gap IS the baseline. It reads '0s' on the first sample, which is precisely the warning the audit's 0.0\" reading needed, and needs no native/wire change. WITHHOLDING the green 'Within acceptance' verdict below a minimum baseline is NOT done — see the needs-decision item below; picking that minimum is a product call. While fixing this I also closed a latent overflow: the All-Sky reticle is a Column that cannot shrink past its own caption, so unlike the TPPA bullseye it overflows rather than squashing when the flex path starves it; its layout floor now reserves a usable reticle slot.
test: 'All-Sky states how long its drift baseline has run' — a 252-second gap between the first and current drift solves renders 'Drift baseline: 4m 12s'.
revert_check: Removed the `if (isAllSky) ...[_buildDriftBaselineCaption(...)]` block — test fails; restored — passes. Correcting my own earlier count: the area's golden failures are FOUR, not two — both cases in polar_alignment/captures_landscape_test.dart and both in flat_wizard/captures_landscape_test.dart. All four are pure pixel diffs (40.6%/40.6%/51.0%/51.2% — whole-screen rasterizer differences from Windows-captured baselines on Linux, per docs/testing/golden-tests.md), the baseline PNGs are unmodified, and grepping the runs for RenderFlex/overflow returns nothing, so none of them is masking a layout regression from the frame-count TextField. All four are @Tags(['golden']) and excluded from `melos run test`.

title: Starting a co-imaging session makes you type RA and Dec by hand with no target lookup
summary: The sheet already prefilled from the framing target when one was set (the finding missed that), but inside the sheet there was no way to resolve a name and no way to take the mount's pointing. Added both, above the RA/Dec fields: 'Look up coordinates' resolves the typed name through targetCoordinateLookupProvider — the app's existing two-source resolver (target library, over the wire on a remote client, then the installed planetarium catalogs) — and applying a match fills the canonical name plus RA/Dec (converting the resolver's RA HOURS to this form's RA DEGREES); 'From mount' fills the centre from mountStateProvider and is disabled with a reason when no mount is connected or it has no coordinates. Both fields stay editable. Noted in the code: the resolver is declared inside the sequencer's Target-editor library and should move to a shared providers/ file — I did not move it because that file is being edited concurrently, and duplicating the two-source search here would be a second thing to keep in step with the catalogs.
test: coimaging_create_sources_test.dart — 'From mount fills the centre from where the scope points' (20.979722h -> 314.6958 deg), 'From mount is unavailable with no mount connected', 'a catalog match fills name and centre in one tap' (and leaves Start session enabled).
revert_check: Replaced the _CoordinateSources row with SizedBox.shrink() — all three tests fail; restored — passes.

(2) The blanket claim is NOT available to an arbitrary member: mosaic_project_controller.dart:569-577 caps a PARTICIPANT at min(participantBulkClaimLimit, half the grid), and _bulkClaimLabel renders 'Claim N panels' for them; only the mosaic's OWNER gets 'Claim all pending' — which is what the audit saw, because it published the mosaic itself. Test 'a participant is not offered an unbounded "Claim all pending"' already asserts this. The 12-hour hold is also already disclosed with the HUB's own expiry (_claimHoldCaption). The one true residual — no 'you hold X of Y' — is fixed as its own item above.

title: Sky Flats has no twilight timing, no sky-brightness gate and no anti-solar pointing
summary: Real and correctly described: the Sky Flats tab offers only Dawn/Dusk, a filter checklist with Auto-Order, a histogram target, a tolerance and a frame count. Nothing on it refers to the sun, to twilight, or to time, even though the app computes civil/nautical/astronomical twilight for the site (the Tonight card shows it) and can slew. But what to build here is a scope call, not a defect: a twilight clock, an ADU-triggered auto-start and a flat-spot slew are three separate features with different risk, and the middle one commands the camera unattended while the last one MOVES THE MOUNT from a calibration screen.
options: (a) Bind the tab to the existing twilight service only — show 'Dusk flats: civil twilight 20:31, usable window 20:35-20:58' with a countdown and an 'arm at' option. Cheap, no new hardware commands, and it fixes the 'when do I press Start' problem, which is the one that actually costs you the window. (b) Add (a) plus an auto-start when the measured sky ADU enters the target band — closes the loop but means the wizard starts exposing on its own. (c) Full NINA parity: (b) plus a 'slew to flat spot' action (anti-solar azimuth, ~75 deg altitude) — best flats, but a calibration screen that slews the mount is a new safety surface (park state, horizon limits, meridian side) and needs its own confirmation and abort story.
recommendation: (a) now, (b) next. The twilight window is the part a user cannot compute in their head at dusk and the part that makes the difference between 6 usable filters and 2; it is pure disclosure of data the app already has, with no new device commands. The anti-solar slew (c) should be a separate, explicitly-confirmed action rather than folded into Start, because the operator may have the scope where it is for a reason.

title: All-Sky: withholding the acceptance verdict until the drift baseline is long enough
summary: The half of the All-Sky finding I did not implement. The reticle prints 'Within acceptance — hold steady' the moment totalError <= threshold, which on a short baseline is a claim about noise: the audit saw 0.0\" (green) at ~8s, then 11 degrees at the next sample. The baseline elapsed time is now shown (fixed above), but the verdict is still ungated, and gating it requires choosing a minimum — which is a judgement about how conservative the wizard should be, not a bug with one right answer.
options: (a) Gate on elapsed drift baseline (e.g. suppress the verdict below 60-120s). Simple and legible, but the right number depends on mount, focal length and solve accuracy. (b) Gate on measurement stability — require N consecutive samples whose total error agrees within the threshold before showing a verdict. Self-calibrating and needs no invented constant, but 'Within acceptance' then appears later than the number does, which needs a caption explaining the wait. (c) Leave it and rely on the new baseline readout to inform the user.
recommendation: (b). It is the only option with no magic number: the wizard already holds AUTO_COMPLETE_HOLD_SECS of consecutive below-threshold samples before it auto-completes (all_sky_polar/mod.rs:312), so applying the SAME consecutive-agreement rule to the on-screen verdict makes the caption and the auto-complete tell one story instead of two. Owner should confirm they want the verdict to lag the number.
